methodologyNotes: Pricing figures were collected from each vendor's public pricing page on the accessedAt date recorded per source. Quote-only or demo-gated vendors carry null price fields with a stated reason; no figure is ever invented. Plans are normalized to the dataset shape regardless of the vendor's native billing model (flat, per-minute, per-call, or hybrid). For per-minute developer platforms, monthlyUsd is the recurring platform fee (0 when pure pay-as-you-go) and overagePerMin is the marginal per-minute rate; minutesIncluded/callsIncluded are null because nothing is bundled. For per-call plans, callsIncluded carries the included quota and overagePerCall the marginal per-call rate; minutesIncluded is null. The cost-at-200-calls normalizer converts every billing model to an effective monthly cost at a chosen call volume and average call length so flat, per-minute and per-call plans can be compared honestly. Annual discounts are recorded as a percentage off the monthly rate where the vendor publishes annual pricing. HIPAA/BAA and integration fields reflect what the vendor states publicly; 'null/unknown' means not published, not absence. AIRA and Upfirst publish byte-identical pricing tables and appear to share a pricing engine; both are recorded with their own sources and a provenance note. This dataset is a static snapshot intended to be refreshed from our scheduled public-page monitoring pipeline.

vendors.provenance: Read from https://smith.ai/pricing/ai-receptionist in a headless browser on 2026-09-09, after the site's own staleness marker had been showing these prices as unverified since 2026-06-27. THE WHOLE LADDER HAD BEEN REPLACED, so this is a rebuild rather than a re-dating. The record held Starter $95 / 30 calls, Basic $270 / 90 calls and Pro $800 / 300 calls at a flat $2.40 per extra call. On the page today there is no Starter and no Basic: the tiers are Free, Pro and Enterprise, each paid tier carrying its own volume selector rather than being one fixed bundle. The entry paid price is $150 for 75 calls, not $95 for 30 — a 58% rise on a bundle two and a half times the size. The name collision was the sharpest risk in the old record: "Pro" now starts at $150, so publishing "Pro (self-service) $800" against today's page actively misled; $800 has moved to Enterprise and out of self-service altogether. The flat $2.40 overage no longer exists either — it is a six-step ladder from $3.00 down to $2.10, and $2.40 appears nowhere on the page. A free tier now exists (25 real calls, $3.00 per call after), which the record did not carry at all. The G2 corroboration this record attached to Starter was dropped with that plan rather than moved onto a successor: it witnessed a tier that no longer exists. A caution for whoever reads this page next: its pricing renders inside shadow roots, so a plain fetch and even a naive rendered read return a few hundred characters of cookie banner while the real page carries about 59,000 — this vendor cannot be checked without piercing them. Smith.ai also publishes a 6-month commitment plan promising rollover calls and a lower rate, with no figure attached, so nothing is recorded for it. Integrations: Clio and Calendly are named on this page today and are kept. MyCase and Filevine were confirmed on the June version of this page and appear nowhere on the rebuilt one; they were dropped rather than carried on a source that no longer says it, and they may well still be supported — the integrations page, not this one, is where that belongs. HIPAA, BAA and Spanish support are not published here.

vendors.provenance: Added 2026-09-09 after CallSprout's founder wrote in with the published figures for Sage, saying plainly that he was not asking for a paid listing. Every one of his six claims was checked against his own pages before anything was published, and every one held: Sage included on both plans, Business $22.95 per user per month, Call Center $39.95, usage $0.39 per minute after the first 30 seconds of each call billed by the second, 24/7 answering that captures the caller's name, number and reason and transfers with that context, and booking that works only against a compatible scheduling API. Nothing had to be rejected, rounded or restated — which is worth recording, because it is unusual. Read from https://callsprout.com/pricing in a headless browser on 2026-09-09; that page carries schema.org Offer markup for both plans at those figures, which is why it is cited rather than the page the founder named. https://callsprout.com/ai/voice-agent carries the identical figures and is attached as a second capture, but it sits on the same host, so it is one publisher saying the same thing twice rather than independent corroboration. No annual term exists on either page — the words annual, yearly and per year appear nowhere and the FAQ states "a simple per-seat price billed monthly" — so annualDiscountPct is null by absence, not by ignorance. Neither page names a single integration partner or makes any compliance claim, so integrations is empty and HIPAA and BAA stay unstated; a free trial exists with no published duration. TWO THINGS A READER MUST NOT BE MISLED BY, both recorded in every plan note. The price is per SEAT while every other vendor in this index prices per business, so $22.95 would otherwise read as the cheapest entry price here when a five-person office pays $114.75. And the modeled cost ignores the 30-second per-call waiver, overstating by $0.195 a call.
